q: Clause 7 of the GCC (Part I) deals with:

options.A: Right of the Railway to Deal with Tenders

q: Under Clause 7, the Railway reserves the right to:

options.B: Reject all tenders only with Railway Board approval
options.C: Accept or reject any tender, in whole or in part, without assigning any reason

q: Under Clause 7 of the GCC, as far as acceptance of tenders is concerned, the Railway is:

options.A: Bound to accept the lowest tender
options.C: Not bound to accept the lowest or any tender
options.D: Bound to accept the highest tender

q: A tenderer whose lowest bid is rejected without reasons given asks for justification. The Railway:

options.A: Must award the work to him
options.C: Is not obliged to assign reasons under Clause 7

q: True or False: The Railway may accept a tender in part.

options.C: The statement is correct only for stores

q: Under Clause 7, the Railway may:

options.A: Divide the work among more than one tenderer
options.B: Award only to a single tenderer in all cases

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Railway's rights under Clause 7?

options.A: The Railway need not assign reasons for rejection
options.B: The Railway may accept a tender in part
options.C: The Railway must accept the lowest tender
options.D: The Railway may reject any tender

q: A tenderer challenges the rejection of his lowest tender in court on the ground that no reason was given. The Railway's stand under Clause 7 is:

options.B: Only the lowest can be rejected with reasons
options.C: Rejection without assigning reasons is permitted

q: True or False: Clause 7 allows the Railway to negotiate with the lowest tenderer.

options.A: The statement is correct for all tenders

q: The right to deal with tenders includes the right to:

options.A: Annul the tender process at any stage
options.B: Extend the tender validity indefinitely without consent
options.C: Change the scope after award without consent

q: A tenderer alleges favouritism because his tender was rejected. Under Clause 7:

options.A: The Railway must prove no favouritism
options.B: The work must be awarded to the complainant
options.C: The Railway's decision to reject without reasons is within its rights
options.D: The tender must be re-evaluated by CBI

q: Which clause gives the Railway the right to reject any tender without assigning reasons?
True or False: The Railway can accept a tender which is not the lowest if it is in the Railway's interest.

options.A: The lowest must always be accepted

q: The phrase 'without assigning any reason' in Clause 7 means:

options.A: The Railway need not explain why a tender was rejected
options.B: The Railway must secretly record reasons
options.C: The CVC must approve each rejection

q: A tender is rejected because the tenderer did not meet eligibility. The tenderer demands the work. The Railway:

options.D: May reject; eligibility is a prerequisite

q: Under Clause 7, can the Railway invite fresh tenders after rejecting all bids?
Which of the following actions is within the Railway's rights?

options.A: Forcing a tenderer to reduce rates
options.B: Awarding without any tender in all cases

q: True or False: A tenderer has a legal right to be awarded the work merely because he quoted the lowest rates.

options.A: The GCC grants such a right
options.D: The statement is correct for open tenders

q: The Railway decides to award the work to the second-lowest tenderer for recorded technical reasons. This is:

options.A: Valid only if the lowest agrees
options.B: Permissible under the Railway's right to deal with tenders
options.D: Permitted only by the Supreme Court

q: Which of the following best sums up Clause 7?

options.B: Tenderers decide who gets the work
options.C: The Railway's discretion in dealing with tenders is wide and final
options.D: The Railway must accept the lowest tender

q: A tenderer seeks the reasons for rejection through RTI. The Railway's tender right:

options.D: Is separate from statutory information rights; Clause 7 only covers the tender decision

q: True or False: The Railway may keep a tender under consideration beyond validity without the tenderer's consent.

options.D: The statement is correct for 30 days

q: If the Railway wishes to extend tender validity, it must:
The decision of the Railway regarding acceptance or rejection of tenders is:

options.D: Final and binding so far as the tender process is concerned

q: Which of the following is correct regarding conditional or incomplete tenders?

options.B: Conditions quoted by tenderers are binding on the Railway
options.C: The Railway may reject a tender that is conditional or incomplete
options.D: The Railway must accept conditional tenders

q: Clause 7A of the GCC provides for:
Under the Two Packet System, the tenderer submits:

options.A: Two copies of the same bid
options.D: Technical bid and Financial bid in separate packets

q: In the Two Packet System, which packet is opened first?
The Financial Bid under the Two Packet System is opened:

options.A: Only of those tenderers found technically qualified

q: The main purpose of the Two Packet System is to:

options.C: Evaluate technical capability without being influenced by prices

q: True or False: In a two-packet tender, the financial bids of technically disqualified tenderers are also opened.

options.C: The statement is correct if rates are low

q: A tenderer submits his rates in the technical packet of a two-packet tender. The consequence may be:
Which of the following correctly describes the two-packet system?

options.A: Packet 1: Technical; Packet 2: Financial; Packet 2 opened only for qualified bidders
options.B: Packets are opened in any order

q: Technical evaluation under the two-packet system is based on:

options.D: The tenderer's experience, resources and eligibility as per tender conditions

q: True or False: The tenderer knows the financial bids of competitors before technical evaluation.

options.B: The statement is correct for open tenders

q: In a two-packet tender, a tenderer is found technically qualified but his financial bid is very high. The Railway:

options.C: May still consider or reject as per its tender rights; price is evaluated among qualified bidders

q: Which of the following is an advantage of the two-packet system?

options.B: Unqualified tenderers are filtered out before price comparison
options.D: Tenders are finalised faster in all cases

q: A tenderer fails to submit the technical packet but submits the financial packet. His tender is:

options.B: Incomplete and liable to be rejected

q: True or False: The two-packet system is used to ensure that price does not influence technical assessment.

options.B: The system is used only for stores

q: Who decides whether a tender will follow single-packet or two-packet system?

options.C: The Railway, as indicated in the tender notice/documents

q: In the Two Packet System, 'Packet' refers to:

options.B: Separate sealed envelopes/submissions for technical and financial offers

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about the two-packet system?

options.A: Financial bids are opened before technical evaluation
options.B: Rates in the technical packet can cause rejection
options.C: Only qualified bidders' financial bids are opened

q: A technically qualified tenderer withdraws before opening of the financial bid. The Railway may:
True or False: E-tenders on IREPS can also follow the two-packet system electronically.
The technical bid generally contains:

options.A: Credentials, experience, resources and documents other than the price offer

q: The financial bid generally contains:

options.C: The price offer / schedule of rates quoted by the tenderer

q: If only one tenderer qualifies technically in a two-packet tender, the Railway:

options.A: May process it as a single tender as per rules
options.C: Must award without opening financial bid
options.D: Must invite him for negotiation only

q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the two-packet system?

options.A: The system applies only to consultancy
options.B: The two-packet system means two rounds of price bidding
options.C: The two packets are opened together
options.D: The two-packet system separates technical evaluation from price evaluation

q: A tenderer quotes his rates in both packets identically. This is:

options.C: A violation that may lead to rejection

q: True or False: The GCC permits the Railway to adopt the two-packet system where considered appropriate.

options.D: Only the Board can permit it

q: Clause 7B of the GCC provides for:
The purpose of a Pre-Bid Conference is to:

options.B: Clarify doubts of prospective tenderers before bidding

q: Clarifications issued during/after a pre-bid conference are generally communicated through:
True or False: Verbal clarifications given in a pre-bid conference automatically modify the tender conditions.
Attendance at a pre-bid conference is:

options.D: As specified in the tender documents (may be optional or mandatory)

q: A tenderer who does not attend the pre-bid conference:

options.B: Is still bound by the clarifications issued

q: Minutes of the pre-bid conference:

options.A: Are issued to all tenderers and form part of the tender documents

q: Which of the following is discussed in a pre-bid conference?

options.A: Scope of work, tender conditions and timelines

q: True or False: A pre-bid conference is usually held before the last date of tender submission.
If a major change emerges from the pre-bid conference, the Railway may:

options.A: Issue a corrigendum and extend the due date if needed

q: A tenderer raises a doubt about contradictory clauses in the pre-bid conference. The correct outcome is:

options.A: A written clarification/corrigendum issued to all
options.C: A private reply to him only

q: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of the pre-bid conference?
True or False: Pre-bid conferences are more common for large and complex works.

options.A: The GCC bans them for large works
options.B: They are held for every small work

q: The venue and date of the pre-bid conference are:
A tenderer cannot attend the pre-bid conference but has doubts. He should:

options.B: Submit written queries as permitted in the tender documents
options.D: Call the Engineer personally for binding clarifications

q: Clause 7C of the GCC relates to:
The Make in India policy in tenders aims at:

options.D: Giving preference to domestic manufacturers and local suppliers

q: Under the Make in India policy, preference is given to:

options.B: Suppliers with prescribed minimum local content
options.D: Tenderers who quote the highest rates

q: 'Local content' under the Make in India policy broadly means:

options.D: The value addition done in India

q: True or False: The Make in India policy is based on government orders issued from time to time.
A tenderer claiming Make in India preference must:

options.B: Furnish the required declaration/certification of local content

q: Which of the following is a likely benefit under Make in India provisions?

options.A: Purchase preference to eligible local suppliers

q: True or False: False declaration of local content can lead to punitive action including banning.
The minimum local content percentages are prescribed by:

options.A: The Government/DPIIT orders applicable to the procurement

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about Make in India in Railway tenders?

options.D: It guarantees award to local suppliers regardless of rates

q: A supplier with 60% local content bids against one with 10% local content. Under the policy:

options.A: The higher local content supplier may get purchase preference as per rules
options.B: The lower content supplier always wins
options.C: Both are treated identically in all cases

q: True or False: Make in India provisions apply in addition to, not in place of, other tender conditions.
The nodal department for Make in India policy orders is generally:

options.B: DPIIT (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade)

q: A tenderer is unsure whether his product meets local content norms. He should:

options.D: Verify as per the policy and certify truthfully

q: Which clause of GCC Part I covers the Make in India Policy?
Clause 7D of the GCC relates to:

options.D: Permission to bid for bidders from countries sharing a land border with India

q: A bidder from a country sharing a land border with India:

options.B: Can bid freely without any restriction
options.C: Requires registration with the competent authority as per government orders

q: The restriction on land-border country bidders is imposed through:

options.A: Government orders on grounds including national security

q: True or False: The competent authority for registration of such bidders is designated by the Government.

options.D: Registration is done by the tenderer himself

q: A bidder from a land-border sharing country participates without the required registration. His bid is:
The land-border restriction applies to:

options.A: Bidders from countries sharing a land border with India

q: Which of the following is a neighbouring country sharing a land border with India (for the purpose of this rule)?
True or False: The rule also covers entities controlled from such countries even if incorporated elsewhere.
A joint venture includes a partner from a land-border country. The JV:

options.B: Must comply with the registration requirement for that partner

q: The purpose of the 7D restriction is primarily:
Which of the following is NOT correct about Clause 7D?

options.B: It applies to bidders from all countries

q: True or False: An Indian company with no foreign control is unaffected by Clause 7D.
The tenderer must declare regarding land-border country association in:

options.A: The prescribed format/declaration with the bid

q: False declaration regarding land-border country links can lead to:
Clause 7D is placed in the GCC to give effect to:

options.A: Government policy on bidders from land-border countries

q: Clause 7E of the GCC relates to:
During evaluation, the Railway may:

options.B: Seek clarifications from tenderers on their bids

q: Clarifications sought by the Railway must:
True or False: A tenderer can revise his quoted rates while giving a clarification.
The purpose of seeking clarification is to:

options.A: Allow tenderers to improve their offers
options.D: Resolve ambiguities without changing the substance of the bid
